name: Saint Hilary of Poitiers
history: A pagan nobleman of Gaul who found his way to Christ by reading the Scriptures, Hilary became bishop of Poitiers and the great defender in the West of the divinity of Christ against the Arians. Exiled to Asia Minor for his faith, he wrote his work On the Trinity there. He is a Doctor of the Church, and the Hilary terms of the English courts and universities take their name from his feast.
life: Hilary was born at Poitiers to a wealthy pagan family and was well educated. Searching for the meaning of life, he read the Old Testament and then the Gospel of John, and was baptised with his wife and daughter. Around 350 the people chose him as their bishop. When the emperor Constantius II pressed the bishops of Gaul to condemn Saint Athanasius and accept an Arian creed, Hilary refused, and in 356 he was exiled to Phrygia. He used the years well, studying the Greek theologians and writing the twelve books On the Trinity. Sent home because he was stirring up too much trouble in the East, he worked to reconcile bishops who had wavered and to restore the faith in Gaul. He was among the first Latin writers of hymns, and he encouraged a young former soldier, Martin, who became Saint Martin of Tours. Pius IX named him a Doctor of the Church in 1851.
prayerTo: Saint Hilary, you sought the truth until you found it in Christ, and you suffered exile rather than deny that He is God. Pray for all who are searching, that they may find the Word made flesh. Pray for me, that I may know my faith, love it and confess it without fear. Amen.
penance: Hilary came to faith through reading Scripture. Give up an hour of screen time today and use part of it to read the first chapter of Saint John’s Gospel slowly.
meditation: He came to Christ by asking what life was for. Ask that question honestly today, and let the opening of John’s Gospel answer it.
